Coach Moment variants: same once-per-match swing, a different shape.
Looks for your coach card and quick chat.
Fixed: the app failing to open on iPhone ("Response served by service worker has redirections").
Fixed: the Moments button covering the third tactic card on iPhone. The command row now gives every button its own slot.
Bots finish the Crystal once a base is open, and only fight defenders who attack or block them.
Ready check: before a match, review your Dojo lineup (heroes, backups, builds, plan) and fix any gaps. You can turn it off.
Every champion can be picked only once per match, across both teams.
Mirror Match (weekly event): both teams get the same five heroes and the same tactic cards. No draft; pure coaching.
Smarter prompts: suggestions only show when you can afford them and the heroes can actually get there in time. Gank prompts name the right ganker.
New: Franchise mode and the Pro League.
New: in-game feedback (Settings and results) and notifications for invites and rematches.
Co-op coaching: two coaches share one team, against AI or 2v2 online. Each runs their own heroes; the lead makes team-wide calls, and the partner can suggest them in one tap.

Game plans: pick Early Aggression, Scale, Objective Control, Split Push or Protect the Carry before the match. Your heroes play to it, it is revealed at kickoff, and you can switch once at halftime. Countering the enemy plan gives +5% damage.
Rival coaches: 12 named AI coaches with their own styles, favourite heroes, draft habits and trash talk. Track your record against each, and beware your nemesis.

Weekly events: Blood Moon, Fog Week, Kami Storm, Golden Waves, Swift Winds, Iron Towers, Shrine Rush and Mirror Match rotate every week. Ranked and cups use only the balance-neutral ones. Choose Classic to skip.
Two new maps: Sunscar Oasis, a desert with dune lairs and a causeway through the oasis, and Mossgate Ruins, a temple city with narrow streets and a pillared plaza.
Weekend Cups: 8-coach online knockouts from Friday to Sunday, with check-ins, a live bracket and trophies on your profile. Real players only.
Fair play: ranked and cup matches are re-checked from their replays. Faked results are rolled back.
Unique skins: every hero has a Signature skin at Mastery 5, and 18 Legendary skins with completely new looks come from achievements, the season pass and ranks. The Dojo has an animated skin viewer.
16 new emotes, new banners and borders, and a signature emote on results and share cards.
34 achievements with rewards, plus a Collection page showing everything you own and how to earn the rest.
Your phone no longer dims or locks during drafts, matches and replays. It sleeps normally again on the menu.
The Moments button keeps its own space in the command row.
Ability effects for all 60 heroes: each element and clan has its own look, with glowing projectiles, trails, dash afterimages and ult symbols on the ground.
Clearer fights: enemy skillshots and area spells show red warnings with a countdown ring, towers draw a line to their target, and low-HP heroes pulse red.
Respawn beams, boss spawn and kill spectacles, and smoother walking, hits and knock-ups. The camera no longer judders.
Living maps: bridges, shore foam, team flags, fish, frogs, fireflies, birds and falling petals, leaves or snow.
Graphics Auto / High / Low. Auto lowers effects detail first on slower phones.
Dynamic music: calm laning, fight tension, Last Stand intensity, an ace fanfare, and victory and defeat stingers.
New sound sets per clan and element. Hits get heavier with damage, objectives roar, and off-screen sounds are quieter and panned.
A limiter keeps phone speakers from distorting. Master, Music, Effects and Menu volume sliders. The game goes silent in the background.
Match Story on results: gold-lead graph, the turning point in plain words, and how your calls went.
Analysis: a timeline of every key moment, damage dealt and taken per hero, call stats and missed chances.
Replay Theater: scrub the timeline, play at 0.5x to 4x, jump to the next fight or objective, follow any hero, and see the fog as either team saw it.
Career stats in your Profile: win rates by hero, build, map and comp, streaks, best calls and personal records.
Friends: add by friend code, from results or from History. See who is online or in a match.
Invite friends to Casual, Lane Rush or Ranked, or share an invite link that opens straight into your lobby.
Rematch after online games, with sides swapped.
Public profiles: tap any coach for their tier, top heroes and recent results.
Leaderboard: Global and Friends tabs, more pages, and your own place pinned.
Fixed: "Ladder offline" when both players reported a result at the same moment.
20 new heroes: 60 in total, 12 per role and clan, each with a kit of its own. Every hero now has a lore line in the Dojo.

4 new builds: Pierce shreds tanks, Siege breaks towers and split-pushes, Spellblade charges your attacks with spells, Warden shields and peels for allies. 11 builds in total, and every hero has at least 3, with a recommended one marked.
New status effects: Silence, Fear, Shred, Mark, Grievous Wounds and Tenacity. Roots now stop dashes. Small, clear markers by the health bar.
Hero duos: 17 pairs get a small bonus fighting side by side, and a DUO combo when they hit the same target.
Team comps: draft 3 or more Dive, Poke, Protect, Split, Teamfight or Pick heroes for a team bonus. The draft shows your comp and duos live.
Coach Moments: Timeout, Rally and All-Out Push. Three big calls, each usable once per match. The AI coach uses them too.
Ranked tiers you can see: Bronze to Kami, with divisions, promotion moments and end-of-season rewards. Kami is earned online.
Hero Mastery 1 to 10: earn titles, badges and color tints for the heroes you coach most.
Find Match now has Ranked, Casual (no rating risk) and Rush queues. Still real players only.
Lane Rush, a new quick mode: one lane, 6 to 8 minute games, on Blossom Bridge and Cinder Run.
Build Guide: a new Dojo tab explaining every build. Long-press any build chip for a one-line summary.
Save clip: turn your Play of the Game into a video you can share.
Smarter teams: a lane-coverage brain sends someone to catch waves, so no lane gets pushed in by minions alone. A "lane open" alert lets you send a hero yourself.
Leashes: minions return to their lane, and monsters and bosses walk home and reset if pulled too far.
Fixed: heroes recalling again and again at the fountain (162 recalls a game down to 34, none wasted).
Smoother movement: about 60% fewer direction reversals, 75% fewer goal flip-flops and 95% less time stuck.
Every hero has a reason: press and hold your hero to see what it is doing and why.
Fixed: enemy towers reaching objective pits and camps. No pit or camp sits in tower range on any map.
Fixed: stretched picture and off taps after leaving the app or rotating the phone.
Fixed: objective icons flickering in the score bar. Each Kami now has its own face.
Fixed: the Auto, Hold and All-In button overlapping the call cards.
Sized for every iPhone from the SE to the 17 Pro Max, including the notch, the Dynamic Island and Safari toolbars.
A new home screen on one landscape screen, with a What's New card.
Hero search and a denser hero grid in the draft and Dojo.
First-match coach tips: four short tips you can skip or replay from Settings.
Juice: caster callouts, hit-stop on big kills, camera punches on ults and Moments, number tweens, menu sounds, and confetti for real wins. Reduced effects turns it all down.
Haptics on kills, objectives and call results where the phone supports vibration. Toggle it in Settings.
Quick chat and emotes in online games, with a mute toggle.
Faster: the app opens instantly on repeat visits and works on a weak signal, first load is 1.1 MB lighter, the HUD does about 70% less work, and slower phones use an adaptive render resolution.
Fixed: the scoreboard and menu stacking up after several matches.
Fairer sides: blue and red now win about equally, after fixing who-acts-first order, mirrored timings and objective pits.
Match pacing: the late game ramps harder, so more matches end at the Crystal before 15:00. The fountain heals only on its platform.
Towers always out-range heroes. Hachi, Tetsu and Brawlo reworked, and every hero and build tuned.
Online: Find Match pairs you with real players (no bots; after 60s it tells you nobody is on). Host/Join stay as private friend games.
Global ladder: ranked matches count only when both players' games agree on the result. Season leaderboard with your rank.
Accounts with no sign-up: your progress saves to the cloud, and a recovery code moves it to another device.
Share links open the game straight on your match card, with the replay.
Dojo: every hero with rating bars (Damage, Toughness, Control, Mobility, Range, Sustain, Difficulty), abilities explained, matchups and skins.
Lineups: 5 saved setups with a backup per role. Your picks lock in automatically; you only choose bans.
Coach's Calls: big moments slow time and give you 2-3 clear choices. Heroes also ask permission for risky plays.
Payoffs: see when a call paid off, or exactly why it failed.
Momentum fills from good play; spend it on a Kami Surge.
Play of the Game, fight cam, and a coach report card after every match.
Cleaner HUD: one decision tray above the calls, one ticker line, and calls that glow when they matter.
Built for phones in landscape: a full-screen installable app (Add to Home Screen), a Menu dropdown, bigger tap targets, a wider camera, and both teams always on screen with enemy respawn timers.

Pro-level AI: calculated tower dives (dives that died for nothing fell from 25% to 8%), respect for unseen enemies, cooldown-aware fights, retreating as a team, no hopeless chases.
Scoreboard: tap the score for every hero's KDA, CS, gold and items. The score bar shows who took each Kami, Oni, Kraken and shrine.
Match history and share cards: show off your wins from the results screen or History.

Lots of juice: hit-stop, ultimate callouts, kill bursts, gold pops, edge alerts, hero chatter, and a Settings screen with colour-blind, text-size and graphics options.
Brand-new calling: six big calls, a hand of tactic cards, and a call ring when you tap the map.

You are the coach. Your five heroes play on their own: they farm, trade, fight and retreat. They only know what your team can see. You win by making the calls.
Ban and pick in turns: Top, Jungle, Mid, Bot and Support. Filter by role or search ("tank", "dive", a name). Green numbers show counters; duos, comps and matching clans give team bonuses.

Pick each hero's build path, 3 tactic cards and a game plan: Early Aggression, Scale, Objective Control, Split Push or Protect the Carry. Your heroes play to it. The recommended plan (★) reads your comp against theirs. Each plan beats two others and loses to two; both plans are revealed at kickoff, and you can switch once at halftime.

Six big buttons along the bottom: Gank, Objective, Push, Shrine, Defend and Regroup. Calls cost charges (max 3, +1 every 20s). Or just tap the map: tap a lane, a pit, a shrine or an enemy and a ring of calls pops up right there.
Your analyst flashes one-tap suggestions ("Mid is overextended: Gank"). Tap the button and the call goes out. Tactic cards (Q, E, T) are one-time plays like Smoke Bomb or Second Wind.

Tap one of your portraits to follow that hero and change its build; tap an enemy portrait to focus them. Press and hold (or right-click) a portrait for details, including "Why": what the hero is doing and why. Good calls build trust, and inspired heroes react faster.

Arrows on the screen edge point at fights, towers under attack and contested objectives: tap one to jump there. The camera follows the action on its own until you drag it, tap the minimap or follow a hero (Cam turns it back on).

Coach's Calls pop up above the buttons when something big is about to happen: pick one of the 2-3 options before the bar runs out. Fill Momentum with calls that pay off, then tap the meter for a Kami Surge.

Moments (M) are three once-per-match calls that open at 1:15: Timeout (reset cooldowns and heal), Rally (+15% damage and speed) and All-Out Push (super minions). The Ults button switches between Auto, Hold (save them for a fight) and ALL-IN. At halftime you can change the game plan, swap a card and adjust builds.

At levels 4, 8 and 12 every hero takes 1 of 2 talents. Set your defaults per hero in the Dojo (hero page or Lineups) or in Prep; on Auto the hero picks for the game it is having, and a quick prompt above the buttons lets you swap it for a few seconds. Tap a portrait to see its talents and, for experts, to swap the next item it buys (Auto stays the default).

A 3-kill streak or an objective taken nearby empowers a hero's next ultimate (gold ring at its feet): bigger, harder, longer. Heroes hold a grudge against whoever killed them last (a little more damage, bonus gold for the payback), rivals trade words, and when both heroes of a duo fire their ultimates within 2 seconds they combine into a duo ult. The Fight Forecast warns you about a fight coming in the next few seconds ("4v3 at Kraken in 8s") from what your team can see: Go or back off with one tap.
Destroy the enemy Shrine Crystal, or have more towers standing when the clock runs out (15:00; Lane Rush: 8:00).

Play vs AI pits you against rival coaches: four per difficulty, each with signature plans, favourite heroes and draft habits. Tap the rival on the Play vs AI card to see them all, pick one, and track your record (beware your nemesis). Play vs AI and the Season Cup move your rating (Bronze to Kami). Find Match pairs you with real players: Ranked climbs the ladder while Casual and Rush never change it. Lane Rush is a quick one-lane game. Host and Join are private games with a friend. Co-op puts two coaches on one team (vs the AI, or 2v2): each runs their own heroes, and the lead makes the team-wide calls (and picks the game plan) while the partner suggests them. Settings has sound, colour-blind colours, text size, reduced effects, graphics quality and a button to replay the first-match coach tips.

Found a club (name, colours, crest) and run it for season after season against seven AI franchises: 14 matches, the top four make the playoffs, then contracts, a rookie draft and free agency. Your roster is your draft: the starting five go straight to prep. Morale, form, fatigue and chemistry give each hero a small edge (a few %, never more than 10%); rest tired starters, keep good heroes playing, and keep pairs together to build bonds. Play every match as the real 5v5, or Sim it. Franchise matches never change your rating. The Pro League tab follows 16 pro teams through a new week-long season every week: predict winners for points and watch the featured matches.
